title: Differential Equations: Order, Degree, Separable and Linear Equations
seo_title: Differential Equations Class 12 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 9)
standard_text: Definition, order and degree, general and particular solutions of a differential equation; solution of differential equations by method of separation of variables, solutions of homogeneous differential equations of first order and first degree; solutions of linear differential equations of the type dy/dx + py = q, where p and q are functions of x or constants, and dx/dy + px = q, where p and q are functions of y or constants (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 12 Differential Equations worksheet (NCERT Chapter 9): order and degree, arbitrary constants, variables separable, particular solutions, homogeneous equations and integrating factors. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Order = highest derivative; degree = its power (if the equation is a polynomial in derivatives).
key_sub: For dy/dx + Py = Q, I.F. = e^∫P dx.
body_html:
How it works

  • Order: the order of the highest derivative. Degree: the power of that derivative, defined only when the equation is a polynomial in its derivatives.
  • The general solution of an equation of order n has n arbitrary constants; a particular solution uses given values to fix them.
  • Variables separable: write g(y) dy = f(x) dx and integrate both sides.
  • Homogeneous: dy/dx = F(y/x); put y = vx.
  • Linear: dy/dx + Py = Q; I.F. = e∫P dx, and y(I.F.) = ∫Q(I.F.) dx + C.
Example

Solve dy/dx + y/x = x².

I.F. = e∫1/x dx = x

xy = ∫x³ dx = x⁴/4 + C

Answer: y = x³/4 + C/x

Common mistakes

  • Taking the highest power as the order.
  • Giving a degree for an equation with sin(dy/dx) in it.
  • Using e^P instead of e^∫P dx for the integrating factor.

faq.q: Does every differential equation have a degree?
faq.a: No. If it is not a polynomial in its derivatives (for example it has sin(y′)), the degree is not defined.
